title: Take a stick-on wall hook off without lifting the paint
instruction: Take the hook off the painted panel without damaging the paint, and put it in the tray.
context: Taking down a stretch-release wall hook is a common household job when redecorating or leaving a rental. Tugging the hook, or peeling its strip away from the wall, can take the paint with it. Here the hook hangs on an uninterrupted painted wall surface and the strip's pull tab lies flat against that surface, as it does on a real wall.
setup: Station table: x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, table top z=0; positions in mm. Wall: one continuous 250 x 1000 x 12.7 mm paper-faced drywall panel (the coupon), primed and painted (finish below), lying face up, centre (270, 0), painted face 62.7 mm above the table, about 2.0 kg. It rests on two pine battens, 30 x 1000 x 50 mm, under x=185 and x=355, and four steel corner clips keep it in place (at each corner two 30 x 8 mm posts stand 0.5 mm outside the edges, and a 3.5 mm thick lip reaches 15 mm over the corner, 0.5 mm above the face); the robot never moves it. Hook: a white plastic medium utility hook, back plate 24 x 62 x 4 mm, stem 14 x 14 x 21 mm; from the stem's top a 14 mm wide, 5 mm thick arm runs 11 mm to the plate's upper end and turns down in a 5 x 6 mm lip; about 15 g. Strip: one 3M Command Medium Refill Strip (17021), white foam, listed 2-3/4 x 3/4 x 1/20 in (70 x 19 x 1.27 mm), both liners removed. Lot A: hook centre line at x=270; the strip's bonded 50 mm lies under the plate from y=-40 to y=+10; the plate runs from y=-40 to y=+22, stem centre y=+4. The other 20 mm is the strip's unbonded pull tab: the same foam, taken as 19 mm wide and 1.27 mm thick like the rest of the strip (the listing gives only the overall size; drawn red in the simulation). It lies flat on the painted face from y=-60 to y=-40, just below the plate, ungripped. Nothing is under or behind the tab but the wall: no gap, edge, notch, spacer or grip aid, and the tab is not lifted or bent beforehand. The painted face continues unbroken to the coupon's ends at y=+/-500; when the last of the strip lets go the tab's end is at y=-365, 135 mm short of the end. Lot B: the coupon with its hook and strip is turned half round in the same clips, so the tab lies from y=+40 to y=+60 and the hook is mirrored. Tray: grey plastic, fixed to the table, inside 100 x 150 mm, walls 4 mm thick and 25 mm high, floor 3 mm, centre (78, 0), empty. The screenshot shows lot A; lots A and B are both run. Finish on every coupon: one coat BEHR Drywall Plus Primer & Sealer No. 73 and two coats BEHR Premium Plus Interior Eggshell Enamel No. 2050 Ultra Pure White, 10 mm nap roller, cured as in reset_notes.
scoring: Each trial scores 0, 0.5 or 1.0; lots A and B are each run once and the two scores averaged. Whole-trial rule first: 0 if any paint under the strip's 19 x 50 mm bond comes away at any time in the trial (afterwards, a photo of the bond area shows missing paint or bare paper). End-state zero rules: 0 if the strip has not let go of the wall along its whole bond (the hook is still stuck on); 0 unless, for the last 1 s, the hook has been let go and still, with every gripper part more than 5 mm from the hook, its strip and tab (video); 0 if the hook rests anywhere but on the coupon, the table or the tray floor with its lowest point within 2 mm of that surface, for example on the tray's rim (ruler). 0.5: none of these applies. 1.0: as 0.5, with the whole hook inside the tray's inner walls and its lowest point within 2 mm of the tray floor (photo from above, ruler). Still means under 10 mm/s. In simulation paint comes away if the hook moves more than 2 mm off the face or more than 4 mm along it before the strip has let go, if a 10 mm length of strip lets go with the tab lifted more than 30 degrees off the face, or if the tab is lifted more than 45 degrees once that length is stretched 30.5 mm or more. A 10 mm length lets go when stretched 61 mm; all five take 305 mm (12 in) of pull. Unreadable hand positions score 0.
reset_notes: 1. Coupons: smooth paper-faced 12.7 mm drywall, 250 x 1000 mm. Roll on one coat of BEHR Drywall Plus Primer & Sealer No. 73, then two coats of BEHR Premium Plus Interior Eggshell Enamel No. 2050 Ultra Pure White, with a 10 mm nap roller at each label's spread rate and recoat time. Use the same product batches for every coupon and log products, coats and the date of the last coat. 2. Cure every coupon at 20-22 degrees C and 40-60% relative humidity for 30 days after its last coat, or the paint maker's full-cure time if that is longer. Touch-dry is not cured. 3. Reuse: after a trial, photograph the 19 x 50 mm bond area. If no paint is missing, the same coupon and position may be used again. If any paint lifted, retire the coupon; do not patch or repaint it. Every trial is therefore run on paint prepared and cured exactly as in steps 1 and 2. 4. Before each trial wipe the bond position with rubbing alcohol and let it dry. Take a new strip. Peel one liner and press the strip onto the back of the hook's plate with the pull tab left clear below the plate; peel the other liner and press the hook onto the wall at the lot's marked position for 30 s. Wait 1 hour. Leave the pull tab lying flat on the wall as it falls; do not lift, bend or thicken it. 5. Clip the coupon in place for lot A or lot B, empty the tray (it stays fixed at its marks) and photograph the start. Record the strip's part number.
fidelity: The coupon lies flat, not upright. The strip is five 10 mm links on 120 N/m springs with a rigid hinged tab; a real foam tab bends and folds when pinched, the rigid one cannot. The 61 mm release stretch, 7.3 N pull and paint-tear limits are uncalibrated rules. Paint is scored only under the bond, not where fingertips slide. Strip size is a distributor's listing; the 50/20 mm bond/tab split and tab thickness are assumed. The hook slides but cannot turn. Masses are numerical. No hardware trial.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 in lot A and 1.0 in lot B (mean 1.0); each trial ended on success after 647 of 800 steps. Dream-1 run: 0.0 in lot A and 0.0 in lot B (mean 0.0); both trials reached the 800-step limit with the hook still on the wall and no paint lifted. Simulation only; no hardware trial.
